title: tenant-scoped-serviceaccounts-and-policy-templates-for-private-upgrades
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce tenant-scoped service accounts and Helm/Terraform policy templating to make Private upgrades safer and reversible. Adds preflight checks and a migration helper. No breaking API changes.
body:
Context and motivation: Private deployments require safer, tenant-isolated RBAC during upgrades. Historically we relied on cluster-level bindings and ad-hoc bootstrap scripts which made upgrades risky for multi-tenant private installs. This PR introduces a composable pattern: tenant-scoped service accounts (namespaced) plus Helm-driven policy templates and Terraform variables so upgrades can be applied with minimal blast radius and an automated migration path for existing cluster-scoped bindings.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add tenant-scoped service account (TSA) controller scaffold and Helm templates to render namespaced ServiceAccount, Role, and RoleBinding per tenant via values.
- Introduce a policy template layer in charts/values: supports per-tenant overrides, KMS binding templates, and map-based grant rules that render to Role objects.
- Extend terraform/modules/private-installer to accept tenant_rbac_policies variable and to write a rendered policy snapshot as an artifact (used by preflight).
- Add helm hooks: rbac-preflight Job (validates API permissions and terraform state lock presence) and upgrade-snapshot hook to persist policy state for rollback.
- Migration helper: a one-shot Job template (migrate-clusterroles-to-namespaced) that attempts idempotent reconciliation of clusterrolebindings into tenant RoleBindings (annotated and reversible).
- Tests: unit tests for template rendering, an e2e scenario using KinD that exercises preflight and migration path, and new lint rules for role name stability.

Commits (summary):
- 7a4d2b3: chart: add tenant policy templating and service account manifests
- c1b9f18: terraform: expose tenant_rbac_policies var and snapshot artifact writer
- e3d5a99: hooks: add rbac-preflight and upgrade-snapshot helm hooks
- b02f8c4: migration: add one-shot migrate-clusterroles-to-namespaced job template
- a8f7c11: tests: template unit tests and kinD e2e for policy migration
- 9c3d4b0: docs: upgrade notes and operational playbook for rollback

Files changed (representative):
- charts/private-installer/templates/serviceaccount-tenant.yaml (new)
- charts/private-installer/templates/role-tenant.yaml (new)
- charts/private-installer/templates/rolebinding-tenant.yaml (new)
- charts/private-installer/values.schema.json (expanded to validate tenant policy map)
- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/rbac-preflight-job.yaml (new)
- helm/README-upgrades.md (updated)
- terraform/modules/private-installer/variables.tf (new var tenant_rbac_policies)
- terraform/modules/private-installer/snapshotter/main.tf (new snapshot writer)
- ops/migrations/migrate-clusterroles-job.yaml (new)
- tests/templates/template_render_test.go (new)

Testing and CI notes:
- CI initially failed on the KinD e2e due to a timing race in the migration Job; I added an exponential backoff with jitter and retried. The pipeline passed on rerun.
- Unit tests for template rendering added; lint checks updated to flag non-deterministic role names.
- Manual validation steps added to docs: run helm upgrade with --set tenantPolicies.<tenant>.enabled=true --set-file tenantPolicies.<tenant>.policy=./policy.yaml then run the preflight hook and confirm snapshot artifact in the Terraform backend.

Review discussion (condensed):
- Liam Chen: requested that role names be stable across upgrades (no hash suffix). Suggested using namespaced stable identifiers and adding a deterministic suffix only when collision detected.
- Author (Aisha): implemented deterministic naming strategy in template_render_test.go and updated values.schema.json to require identifier field.
- Sara Voss: asked for explicit instructions for rollback when migration partially applies to avoid orphaned ClusterRoleBindings. Added upgrade-snapshot and annotated migration jobs with reversible labels and a 'dry-run' toggle.
- Omar Rasul: raised concern about Terraform state locks when snapshotting; CI initially did not check remote state lock. I added a check in rbac-preflight Job to validate state lock and fail fast if lock is not present. Omar approved after the check and an added integration test.

Merge strategy and outcome:
- After two approvals and CI green, PR was squashed and merged into release/2.3 on 2026-03-04. Merge method: squash.

Post-merge actions and follow-ups:
- Created ENG-1529 to build an automated 'migration-operator' that can run the reconcile path across large clusters and report per-tenant migration status.
- Ops runbook updated at docs/private-installer/upgrade-playbook.md with step-by-step for preflight, migration, and rollback.
- Request to release a patch chart v2.3.1 is open (release PR will reference this merge).

Operational considerations and backward compatibility:
- The new flow is opt-in via tenant_policies in Helm values and Terraform var. Existing installs that do not set tenant policies remain unchanged.
- Migration Job is idempotent and annotated; it does not delete cluster-scoped bindings by default. Operators must review the migration snapshot before promoting deletions.

Notes for reviewers of future related PRs:
- Keep role names stable by default; avoid adding autogenerated hashes unless explicitly required.
- Ensure any Terraform snapshot writer uses the same backend configuration as the cluster (do not assume local state).
- Preflight must validate both API server RBAC and the Terraform lock file to prevent interleaved upgrades.

If you want a quick demo: check the branch feature/private-tenant-sa-policy-upgrade, run the helm chart against a KinD cluster with the sample values in charts/samples/tenant-policy.yaml and then run the migrate-clusterroles-to-namespaced Job in ops/migrations with dry-run=false to observe annotations and snapshot output.

Acknowledgements: thanks to Omar for the Terraform lock check, Liam for role-naming guidance, and SRE on-call for early migration validation during the canary.
